check1.q: How are you paid, unless your offer states a different rate?
o: By your client, at a rate you agree with them
By Relève, at $7 an hour, as a fixed monthly amount worked out from your agreed hours
By Relève, for each task you finish
By a payroll company, every week
check1.w: Relève pays you directly, from its own funds, once a month. The standard is $7 an hour, paid as a fixed monthly amount worked out from the hours your role is agreed at. Your client never pays you.

check1.q: Your client asks how much you are paid. What do you say?
o: Ask them what they pay Relève
Say kindly that pay is handled by Relève, and they are welcome to ask their Client Success Manager
check1.w: Pay stays private in both directions. You never discuss your pay with a client, and you never ask what the client pays.

check1.q: Your client asks you to work three extra hours this weekend. What do you do?
o: Tell your Talent Success Manager first, and only work extra hours once they agree
Do it and add it to your invoice
check1.w: Never work extra hours or overtime without your Talent Success Manager agreeing first.

check1.q: A client says they would like to hire you directly, outside Relève. What do you do?
o: Accept, since it is your choice
Thank them and tell your Talent Success Manager
check1.w: During a placement and for 12 months after it ends, you can’t work with that client outside Relève. Telling your Talent Success Manager is always the right move.

check1.q: Which AI tool use is allowed?
o: Any free AI tool, with any client information
A tool your client has approved, that does not train on what you type
Any tool, as long as you delete the chat after
check1.w: Only client-approved tools, and never a tool that uses your inputs to train its models. Always check the result yourself.

check2.q: You open your task list in the morning. What does your client see?
o: That each task they gave you has been seen, with the time
check2.w: Opening your list marks your client’s tasks as seen, and they see when.

check2.q: You finish a task your client assigned. What happens next?
o: It goes to your client for review, and they accept it or send it back with a note
It goes into your end of week report automatically
check2.w: A finished client task is sent for review. A task sent back comes with a note and rises to the top of your list.

check2.q: You don’t understand what a task needs. What is the best move?
o: Guess and hope for the best
Use Ask a question on the task
check2.w: Ask a question moves the task to waiting for your client and emails them. It is always better than guessing.

check2.q: Which of these does your client never see?
o: Your end of week report and any concerns in it
A highlight you chose to share
check2.w: Your daily log, end of week reports, concerns and anything you tell your Talent Success Manager stay with Relève.

check2.q: When should you read Your briefing?
o: Before your first day, and again whenever it changes
check2.w: Your briefing holds your client’s tools, access and preferences. Read it before day one and keep up with changes.

check3.q: A task will not be ready by its date. What do you do?
o: Say nothing and finish it late
Tell your client before the date passes, with a new date you can keep
Ask Relève to change it quietly
check3.w: Never let a date pass quietly. An early, honest update with a new date keeps trust.

check3.q: You sent a document to the wrong person. What is the best response?
o: Tell your client quickly, fix what you can, and explain how it won’t happen again
check3.w: Tell them fast, fix it, and prevent it. If it involves personal or confidential data, also tell your Talent Success Manager within 48 hours.

check3.q: Which update is easiest for a busy client to act on?
o: A long story of everything you did today
“Done: the proposal is sent. In progress: travel options, ready by 3 pm. Need from you: a yes on the venue by tomorrow.”
check3.w: Short and complete: what is done, what is in progress, and what you need from them.

check3.q: How often do you have a call with your Talent Success Manager on a full-time Essential role?
o: Only when there is a problem
check3.w: Weekly on Essential roles, and every two weeks on part-time Starter roles.

check3.q: Your client keeps asking for evening work outside your agreed hours. What do you do?
o: Raise it with your Talent Success Manager, and note it as a concern in your end of week report
check3.w: Never argue with a client and never carry a problem alone. Raising a concern is never held against you.
